Bazar Pe Bazar Guzarte Rahe Qaidi Write Up
Bazar Pe Bazar Guzarte Rahe Qaidi.
Har Mor Pe Jeete Rahe Marte Rahe Qaidi.
Rasi Ne Unhein Aik Bana Rakha Tha Lekin.
Tasheer Ki Zarbat Se Bikharte Rahe Qaidi.
Zakhmon Mein Badal Deti Thi Pairon Ke Jo Chale.
Marham Bhi Ossi Khak Ko Karte Rahe Qaidi.
Pani Tu Muyasar Na Tha Bas Ashk The Jin Ko.
Abbas Ke Mashkezay Mein Bharte Rahe Qaidi.
Girna Isse Kehte Hain Keh Aye Logo Utarna.
Chalte Howay Naqon Se Utarte Rahe Qaidi.
Mil Jaye Na Iss Waqt Koi Janne Wala.
Bazar Mein Iss Baat Se Darte Rahe Qaidi.
Tauheed Ko Chalne Mein Na Dushwari Ho Akbar.
Kharon Pe Qadam Iss Liye Dharte Rahe Qaidi.

from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = 'src/data/lyrics/bazar-pe-bazar-guzarte-rahe-qaidi-tajpoints-5abd28dde8577465fca5.md'
old = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'HEAD:{p}'], text=True).split('---')[2].strip().splitlines()
_, front, body = Path(p).read_text().split('---')
roman = front.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1].strip().splitlines()
source = body.strip().splitlines()
assert roman[0] == '1' and source[0] == '۱'
assert [line.strip() for line in roman[1:]] == [line.rstrip('.').lower().replace('abbas', 'Abbas').replace('akbar', 'Akbar') for line in old[2:]]
assert len(roman) == len(source) == 15
print('Verified 14 matching verse positions and preserved Roman wording.')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 14 verses in Urdu script and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. Both editions retain the original verse order and single stanza. Updated the title and text direction, and removed the `noUrdu` tag.

I treated “Write Up” as a heading and read “chale” as چھالے and “naqon” as ناقوں. Only the selected Markdown file was edited.
